canyons.note: Grade: V3 A3 I ★ Slippy gorge walking with some optional bigger features. This is a open canyon with constant escape out along the bank. Paddled in a kayak after rainfall (grade 5).

canyons.name: Allt a’Bhealaich
canyons.note: Can you help add information for this canyon? use the amend page and quote this canyons name.

canyons.name: Rhaeadr Ogwen
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A2 II ★ Easy access leads to a short, open canyon with down climbing, shallow pools and 3 abseils.

canyons.name: Whillan Beck
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A4 I ★★ Low angle canyon in an easily accessed valley. Lots of deep pools, jumps and slides to enjoy in a stunning setting.

canyons.name: Nant Lago
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A3 IV ★★ An interesting canyon with 2 distinct sections – the upper section is composed of big open falls/slides. The lower section is an impressive walled in gorge.

canyons.name: Dundonnell Canyon
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A4 IV ★★★★ Short access leads to 40m high walls, jumps and raps.

canyons.name: Batchelors Burn
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A2 II ★ This cold mountain burn features two exciting rappels interspersed with a long, mellow (but scenic) gorge walk through birch and pine forest.

canyons.name: Falls of Chia-aig
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A4 II ★★★ A fully featured adventure canyon with some enclosed sections and multiple quality features. Long sections of gorge walking separates more exciting features.

canyons.name: Prysor
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A3 II ★★ The most popular canyon in North Wales. Best after rainfall when all the slides are pumping and even better after a few trips or with a guide once you know the best way to descend features.

canyons.name: Bracklinn Falls
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A4 I ★ A short jumping canyon with no abseils or slides.

canyons.name: Dalroy Canyon
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A2 I ★★ An easy access short canyon, with abseils, jumps, slides and atmospheric gorge walking.

canyons.name: Cwm Llechen
canyons.note: Can you help add information for this canyon? use the amend page and quote this canyons name.

canyons.name: Inchree Falls
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A3 II ★★ A easy access, high flow and well equipped canyon with slides, jumps and abseils. Can be busy in the summer months.

canyons.name: Nether Beck
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 II ★ Usually ascended, featuring deep pools and a cave to explore.

canyons.name: Pistyll Cain
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 II ★ Quality scrambling and 10m abseil, before the main falls (Pistyll Cain). There is a cave midway on Pistyll Cain with an entrapment hazard to watch out for.

canyons.name: Finglen Burn
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A3 III ★★ A fun trib to gorge scramble with lots of abseils in the tributary and a few jumps in the gorge scramble at the bottom

canyons.name: Sutherlands Grove
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A4 III ★ ★ A spectacular and slippery well sculpted gorge formed into the Pelite bedrock.

canyons.name: Shaggie Burn
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A2 I ★ An open adventure canyon with multiple drops.

canyons.name: Doe
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A4 II ★★★ Good tracks lead to a fully featured, escapable canyon. One of the best canyons in England

canyons.name: Crook Ghyll
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A1 I ★ Unassuming at entry, this canyon is a lovely, short collection of abseils and downclimbs, with short enclosed sections.

canyons.name: Allt Aireimh
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A2 II ★ A short, low flow canyon with short slides, small jumps and medium height rappels. A 13m corkscrew abseil is the main feature.

canyons.name: Afon Arddu
canyons.note: Grade: V6 A6 II ★★ Wait for a drought or extremely dry period before descending this canyon. Expect strong flows and lots of recirculating currents even during dry periods.

canyons.name: Mill Gill
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A2 I ★ Short gorge scramble with an impressive abseil

canyons.name: 0 Star Canyon
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A1 Gorge/ ghyll scramble with limited – no interest. – Sol Armer

canyons.name: Teigl
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A3 I ★ Interesting gorge scrambling/ walk, sections separated. Some roped sections near the start and possible jump options along the way.

canyons.name: Sligachan Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 I ★★ A short approach leads to an escapable canyon with jumps, slides and abseils.

canyons.name: Coe Canyon
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A2 II ★ A long, high flow canyon with some interesting features separated by scrambling through a deep gorge.

canyons.name: Finlas Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 II ★ ★ A short and scenic slot canyon with two abseils. Perfect for experienced leading inexperienced.

canyons.name: Strathcarron
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A3 II ★ ★ A fully featured Canyon with large watershed and good flow.

canyons.name: Gleann Mor
canyons.note: Can you help add information for this canyon? use the amend page and quote this canyons name.

canyons.name: Afon Sychryd
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A4 ★ A popular high flowing gorge with plenty of jumps and slides. No form of rope work is permitted in this canyon – See notes below

canyons.name: Falls of Falloch
canyons.note: Not a canyon but a popular cliff jumping spot if you’re in the local area. check pool carefully before jumping due to underwater ledges.

canyons.name: Hell Gill
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A2 III ★★ An incredible, inescapable slot canyon with 10m high walls, short access and a good fun to effort ratio.

canyons.name: Brig O Turk
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 I ★★ Short canyon with small jumps and one larger pitch (or jump).

canyons.name: Strone
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A3 III ★★ A fully featured adventure canyon with plenty of features separated by long scrambles.

canyons.name: Fairy Glen
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A5 II ★★ Stunning environment with some very delicate biodiversity. Becomes deadly in moderate – high flows.

canyons.name: Trough Head Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A1 II A nice short gorge section. Rock formations within the gorge are quite interesting. A light flow required to make short flat slides work. Main feature is a short 2m – 3m waterfall into a large swimming pool. No jumps, abseil

canyons.name: 0 Star Canyon
canyons.note: Insignificant gorge, not sure if it’s had a full descent. Super slippy and overgrown ditch. A section may be used by the neighbouring outdoor centre. – Sol Armer

canyons.name: Middle & Lower Cynfal
canyons.note: ⛔️ This canyon is closed – Recreational a ccess is not permitted in the canyon, current discussions may lead to further restrictions and fines. For more info click view more.

canyons.name: Mincer
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A4 I No Stars Quality scrambling. Handline could be useful in places.

canyons.name: Dewerstone Gorge
canyons.note: A scenic gorge scramble used by local activity centres.

canyons.name: Angletarn Beck
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A1 I ★ A low flowing gorge scramble, with shallow pools and small waterfalls to climb.

canyons.name: 0 Star Canyon
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A1 Mountain ghyll scramble. Dry in dry weather. Water can get too high for ascent after an intense amount of rain. Anchors are limited. Given a grade 2 in scrambling guidebooks. Sol Armer

canyons.name: Moss Force
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A2 I ★ An open canyon with multiple drops.

canyons.name: Bridge of Brown
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A3 II ★★ Easy access leads to a sculpted high quality gorge with smooth narrow walls, deep pools, jumps and slides.

canyons.name: Cawdor Canyon
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 IV ★★ Deep conglomerate slot canyon, with committing and atmospheric gorge walking

canyons.name: Meig Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A3 I ★★ A popular kayak run with some sliding and jumping options in an impressive bedrock gorge.

canyons.name: Rumbling Bridge
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A3 II ★ A deep, narrow gorge scramble fed by a massive catchment.

canyons.name: Heavy Metal Canyon
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A2 II ★★ A steep canyon cutting the crag in half at the head of Coledale. Spectacular views of the northern fells over the old mine workings.

canyons.name: 0 Star Canyon
canyons.note: Slippy scramble/ abseil of little to no interest. – Sol Armer

canyons.name: Calvine Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A3 I ★★ A high flow gorge walk with deep pools, optional raps slides and jumps.

canyons.name: How Stean Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 II ★ An abseil into the gorge from a bridge. Then a wet gorge scramble with deep swimming pools. Descents must be with a guide and cost up to £160 pp

canyons.name: Rheidol
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A6 V ★ A gorge walk with a few drops/ abseils. Also grade V+ kayak descent. Recommend very low levels to run this.

canyons.name: Duror
canyons.note: Grade: V4 A2 II ★ A steep approach leads to a short, scenic canyon, featuring two long abseils though a sculpted quartzite slot.

canyons.name: Monessie Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 I ★★ A popular gorge with deep pools, sculpted walls and a single abseil

canyons.name: 0 Star Canyon
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A1 Ghyll scramble with a few intermittent steeper drops of little interest. Difficult anchors if you choose to descend the falls, alternatively climb around. – Sol Armer

canyons.name: Black Rock Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A5 IV ★★★ A long, deep committing canyon, one of the best trips in the UK.

canyons.name: Finnich Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A2 IV ★ A 30m deep, inescapable gorge walk with jumps and slides.

canyons.name: Hudeshope Beck
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A1 I Only one technical element, a 3m or 4m slide or jump from river right on the only sizeable cascade.

canyons.name: Lui Water
canyons.note: V2 A4 I ★ A short, medium/high flow river with small slot sections.

canyons.name: Pont Rhyd Y Groes
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A2 II ★★ A deep aquatic well sculpted gorge with slides and jumps, perfect for the advanced leading novices.

canyons.name: Clydach Gorge
canyons.note: Grade: V2 A1 I ★ A wooded low flowing gorge scramble with two main waterfalls to climb, best as a beginners introductory trip.

canyons.name: Reahope Burn
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A1 II ★ A VERY short trip to ascend a couple of falls, good as an introductory trip, not worth doing if you are with an experienced group

canyons.name: Waterfall Country
canyons.note: Grade: V1 A2 II A descent down a large river, Abseiling is not allowed in this river therefore the elements that cannot be jumped, slid or scrambled must be avoided.

canyons.name: River Mellte
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A2 I ★ The largest section in the neath valley with big jumps and slides. Trips are often ascents rather than descents. *No Rope work permitted

canyons.name: Tummel
canyons.note: Grade: V3 A2 I ★ ★ A short approach leads to a steep technical descent with 14 pitches.
